title: Monday Teacher Plan
note: Short week: Mon, Thu, Fri only. Expectations Wayground + grade check today. One turn-in each: the exit ticket. 6th/7th read + predict today; Friday (your observation) they break their bridges.

4th Period.topic: Juice Week, Day 1: plan your paddle-hit juice
4th Period.goal: By the end of class, I can explain what juice is and plan the juice my game shows when the ball hits my paddle.
4th Period.exitTicket: What juice will your game show when the ball hits your paddle, and how will it make the player feel?
prep: Create the Google Classroom assignment 'Juice Week' and attach the Day 1 handout; post the exit ticket
Optional: a 60-second no-juice vs juicy clip (e.g. Block Breaker vs. any juicy breakout) ready to play
Your live base game open to demo the 'no juice' paddle hit

segments.title: Wayground: classroom expectations
segments.do: Students take the expectations Wayground.
segments.why: Monday routine: predictable start (Maslow: safety).
tips: No review Blooket on Mondays.

segments.title: Review answers + today's goal
segments.do: Go over the most-missed expectations, then read the goal: By the end of class, I can explain what juice is and plan the juice my game shows when the ball hits my paddle.
segments.why: Students know the target.
tips: Point to the goal again halfway through and at the exit ticket.

segments.title: Grade check
segments.do: Infinite Campus, find the overall grade, fill out the Weekly Grade Check-In form.
segments.why: Weekly self-monitoring.
tips: Keep grades private.
Below 70%: regrade form + Tuesday tutoring 3:15-4:00.
Exit tickets can't be redone; missing work is accepted late for full credit.

segments.title: This week and the points
segments.do: Mon plan, Thu build, Fri play + DONUTS vote + turn in once. Show the points: 55 turned in, 15 boxes, 15 juice words, 15 juice is live.
segments.why: Safety first: they see how to get 85 even if the game breaks.
tips: Say it plainly: Friday's vote is for the best GAME, so juice is how you win it.

segments.title: Mini-lesson: juice, revisited
segments.do: Show the no-juice vs juice picture (or clip). Define juice, feedback, responsive, player action. Key rule: delete the juice and the game still works.
segments.why: I do: shared vocabulary before design.
tips: Ask: 'Did the rules change between the two?' (No, only the feel.)
Mention the Composite tie: one command, every brick blinks.

segments.title: We do: rate the paddle hit
segments.do: Everyone plays their live game 1 minute, thumbs 1-5 on how much the paddle hit feels like it matters. Partners name what the game shows on a hit.
segments.why: Students feel the problem before they solve it.
tips: Answer: nothing new happens; the ball just turns around.
10-2: turn and talk here.

segments.title: You do: plan the juice
segments.do: At least 2 kinds of juice on the paddle hit, with color and duration. Say it out loud to a partner; partner checks the rules didn't change.
segments.why: Design first; Copilot builds Thursday.
tips: Stuck: flash yellow + squash for a quarter second.
Redirect anything that changes speed/score: that's a mechanic, not juice.
Sound = Future Engineer only, headphones first.

segments.title: Exit ticket
segments.do: Typed on Google Classroom with frames.
segments.why: One turn-in.
tips: Full answer: 2 named effects + color/duration + a 'because' about feedback/responsiveness.

watchFor: Plans that change the rules (faster ball, more points): steer back to the look.
Students who can't load their live game: hard refresh, then the base game link.
Copy-paste plans: ask them to say it out loud in their own words.

6th Period.topic: Breaking Things on Purpose: reading + break prediction
6th Period.goal: By the end of class, I can explain tension and compression and use them to predict where my group's bridge will break on Friday.
6th Period.exitTicket: Where will your bridge break first on Friday, how many bottles will it hold, and why?
prep: Handout printed (4 pages), one per student; Google Classroom assignment 'Break Test' with exit ticket posted
A paper strip per pair for the squeeze/stretch demo
Bridges handed back to table groups for the last segment

segments.title: Wayground: classroom expectations
segments.do: Students take the expectations Wayground.

segments.title: Review answers + today's goal

segments.title: This week and the points
segments.do: Mon read + predict, Thu final prep, Fri BREAK TEST until it fails, turn in once.
segments.why: Students hear Friday's payoff up front (motivation).
tips: Say: Friday you finally get to break it.

segments.title: Key words: paper strip
segments.do: Every pair pulls a paper strip (holds = tension), then pushes its ends (buckles = compression). Pre-teach compression, tension, buckle, failure load.
segments.why: ELD: hear, say, do each word before reading it.
tips: Ask: which is stronger, pulled paper or pushed paper? Why do engineers double the squeezed parts?

segments.title: Partner reading
segments.do: 5 chunks. Younger reads aloud, older summarizes ('This part says...'), swap every chunk. 3s: Word Finder.
segments.why: Reading closely (ELD.PI.6-8.6); summarizing is the 10-2 processing.
tips: Circulate and listen to summaries; publicly praise a precise one.
Mid-lesson: point to the goal again.
Check: after Chunk 2, ask the class which chord is squeezed (top).

segments.title: Find T and C on your bridge
segments.do: Groups point to their top chord (compression) and bottom chord (tension), find the Test 1 X and the cardboard fix (Thursday), and agree on where it breaks first.
segments.why: Transfer the reading to their own design.
tips: Push for a reason, not a guess: 'it is squeezed and thin, so it will buckle'.

segments.title: Exit ticket: predict the break
segments.do: Each student types a prediction: spot, number of bottles, reason, with frames.
segments.why: One turn-in; Friday's comparison depends on it.
tips: Full answer: a named spot + a bottle number + tension/compression + buckle/tear/pop.
Save these: on Friday students compare them to the break.

watchFor: Students copying a groupmate's exit ticket word for word: same spot is fine, own words required.
Readers rushing: Summarizer must say it back before the next chunk.
Groups that skip the bridge look: the prediction must point to their own bridge.

accommodations: Agenda on the board, goal reviewed after the Wayground and mid-lesson, numbered steps, worked example first, checklists, sentence frames, positive reinforcement, frequent check-ins.
Key words with pictures (juice/feedback, cam/follower, gusset), partner talk before writing, two sentence frames, Immersive Reader.
Lexend Deca, large type, steps read aloud, speech-to-text OK, spelling not graded.
Short timed chunks with a visual timer, hands-on roles (Cutter, Gluer, Measurer), seating near the demo, discreet redirection, break pass.
Extended time; floor version: 8th one juice effect, 7th one fix piece on the X, 6th frame with holes even if not glued; dictated exit tickets; intentional partners; calm-down space.
frameworks: 8th builds toward a DONUTS vote Friday; 6th/7th predict today and break their bridges Friday.
Birthday-order roles with real authority; publicly assign competence to precise measurers and sharp inspectors.
Points and floor up front, one turn-in, predictable short-week routine, 'you are not behind'.
Mon Understand/Plan, Thu Apply/Create, Fri Evaluate.
